metadata.title: Panitumumab 6mg/kg and Modified FOLFOX-6 Therapy -14 day
metadata.indication: First-line treatment of adult patients with wild-type RAS metastatic colorectal cancer.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.schedule_summary: A 14-day cycle: panitumumab, oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil start on Day 1, followed by a fluorouracil pump lasting about 46 hours. Arrange disconnection around Day 3. Continue according to benefit and tolerance.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Source-mapped NCCP 00447 v7; independent clinical/pharmacy validation remains pending. Use the current source and individual clinical judgement.

rule_engine.conflict_policy: Use the most restrictive overall action; combine component changes using the greatest reduction per component rather than summing reductions.
rule_engine.missing_data_policy: Evaluate only supplied values; do not infer missing values. Eligibility/context fields remain optional unless a specific rule requires them.

neuropathy_grade.label: Peripheral neuropathy grade
neuropathy_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess sensory and/or motor symptoms and their effect on instrumental versus self-care activities of daily living. Distinguish transient cold sensitivity from persistent functional neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No peripheral sensory or motor neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only. CTCAE v5.0 grades symptomatic paraesthesia separately when that is the more accurate term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate symptoms that limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms that limit self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

unexplained_respiratory_symptoms.label: New or worsening unexplained respiratory symptoms

diarrhoea_current_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade
diarrhoea_current_grade.assessment_guidance: Use NCCP 00447 table 6 source grading. Its legacy stool/ostomy bands differ from CTCAE v5; mild ostomy change overlaps grades 1–2 and needs clinical adjudication.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No diarrhoea

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase 2–3 stools/day; mild watery ostomy increase

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase 4–6 stools/day or nocturnal stools; mild watery ostomy increase (source overlap)

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase 7–9 stools/day, incontinence, malabsorption or severe watery ostomy increase

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Increase ≥10 stools/day, grossly bloody ostomy output, parenteral-support requirement or dehydration

diarrhoea_highest_grade.label: Highest diarrhoea grade since previous cycle
diarrhoea_highest_grade.assessment_guidance: Use NCCP 00447 table 6 source grading. Its legacy stool/ostomy bands differ from CTCAE v5; mild ostomy change overlaps grades 1–2 and needs clinical adjudication.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No diarrhoea

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase 2–3 stools/day; mild watery ostomy increase

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase 4–6 stools/day or nocturnal stools; mild watery ostomy increase (source overlap)

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase 7–9 stools/day, incontinence, malabsorption or severe watery ostomy increase

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Increase ≥10 stools/day, grossly bloody ostomy output, parenteral-support requirement or dehydration

stomatitis_current_grade.label: Current stomatitis grade
stomatitis_current_grade.assessment_guidance: Inspect the oral cavity and assess pain, ulceration, diet modification and whether oral intake is impaired.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

rash_grade.label: Current panitumumab skin toxicity grade
rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade the dermatological reaction clinically, not acne alone. Record the number of severe episodes and response after withholding. Blistering, skin detachment or infection requires urgent assessment.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No acneiform rash.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Papules/pustules covering under 10% body-surface area, with or without pruritus or tenderness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Papules/pustules covering 10-30% body-surface area with or without symptoms and psychosocial/instrumental-ADL impact, or over 30% with mild symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Papules/pustules covering over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, limiting self-care ADL, or local superinfection requiring oral antibiotics.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, or extensive superinfection requiring IV antibiotics.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion reaction grade
infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Document timing, symptoms, need to interrupt treatment, response to symptomatic therapy, recurrence, hospitalisation and any airway or haemodynamic compromise.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

ocular_symptoms.label: New eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blurred vision

magnesium_mmol_l.label: Magnesium
magnesium_mmol_l.assessment_guidance: Interpret against the local range and symptoms. Set electrolyte abnormality when correction is needed; this regimen has no source-defined numerical hold threshold.

skin_occurrence.label: Number of episodes of grade ≥3 skin toxicity

skin_doses_withheld.label: Doses withheld for this skin episode

skin_failed_recovery.label: Not recovered after the planned 1–2 dose withholding period

severe_skin_complication.label: Severe skin infection, blistering or skin detachment

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Panitumumab is low risk; the chemotherapy combination is driven by oxaliplatin, which is moderate risk (NCCP V6 table 7).
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
supportive_care.premedication: Not routinely required for panitumumab; local policy after reactions. Chemotherapy antiemetics follow NCCP/local regimen risk.
other_supportive_care: Pre-emptive skin care, sun protection and prescribed therapy under local EGFR policy.
Monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before/during treatment and for up to 8 weeks after; NCCP specifies monthly electrolytes for 2 months post treatment.
Review eye symptoms, lung symptoms, skin infection and diarrhoea; give urgent contact plan.

monitoring: Validated extended RAS wild-type result; confirm first-line metastatic indication, ECOG and organ function.
FBC, renal and liver profile; DPD test before fluorouracil. Interpret uracil cautiously in renal impairment and consider genotype confirmation.
Baseline electrolytes, magnesium and calcium; neuropathy, hearing/vision, skin and respiratory symptoms; access and pump assessment.
FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle. Review diarrhoea, mucositis, neuropathy, infection, skin and infusion effects.
Check magnesium/calcium/potassium and correct abnormalities according to the local EGFR monitoring plan.
Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last panitumumab dose.
Assess cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy and cold sensitivity throughout treatment and after stopping; disease scans follow the consultant plan.
